title: Compiler Design
description: Learn to build professional compilers, lexers, AST engines, and target code generators.

lessons.title: Introduction to Compilers
lessons.content: A compiler is a specialized system program that translates source code written in a high-level language into machine code or intermediate representations. It consists of two main divisions: the Front-End (lexical analysis, parsing, semantic verification) and the Back-End (optimization, code generation). Understanding compilation theory provides vital insight into memory footprints and program optimization.

lessons.title: Core concepts of Compilation
lessons.content: The translation process relies on formal grammars. We represent source structures using Regular Expressions (for identifiers and literals) and Context-Free Grammars (for statement nests and arithmetic). Symbol tables coordinate identifiers and scopes during compilation phases.

lessons.title: Syntax Analysis & DFAs
lessons.content: Lexical analyzers utilize Deterministic Finite Automata (DFAs) to group source character matrices into Lexeme sequences. If a stream matches predefined rules, it generates tokens. Otherwise, lexer warnings raise syntax exceptions. Practicing tree generation strengthens algorithmic scope comprehension.

title: DBMS
description: Master database schemas, query optimization, normal forms, and transaction ACID parameters.

lessons.title: Introduction to Databases
lessons.content: Database Management Systems (DBMS) allow users to store, query, and modify structured tables. Relational systems represent entities in grids called relations. By structuring indexes, users can speed query evaluation dramatically.

lessons.title: Entity-Relationship Diagrams
lessons.content: Entity-Relationship Models capture real-world constraints via rectangles (entities), ovals (attributes), and diamonds (relationships). Drawing clear schemas avoids data modeling errors down the line.

lessons.title: 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF Normalization
lessons.content: Database Normalization is the systematic optimization of tables to restrict data duplication. 1NF guarantees scalar elements. 2NF guarantees that non-key elements depend entirely on the composite keys. 3NF removes transitive dependencies to protect referential integrity.

title: Operating Systems
description: Study kernel loops, process thread context-switches, CPU schedules, and virtual memory segments.

lessons.title: Monolithic vs Microkernel
lessons.content: A kernel sits directly above the hardware layer. Monolithic kernels (like Linux) embed virtual file systems, device drivers, and schedulers inside a unified space. Microkernels (like Mach) push drivers and file systems to user-space, improving system modularity.

lessons.title: CPU Scheduling Loops
lessons.content: CPU schedulers allocate execution threads. Shortest Job First minimizes average wait indexes but risks starvation. Round Robin cycles processes using a fixed time quantum to provide highly interactive multitasking platforms.
